prompt.context: Our client is a retailer in New York State. They have 120 stores across the state and they are constantly competing with other retailers for customers. They are NOT a low-cost retailer in the state but on certain days they give out heavy discounts on their products to attract customers. They create brochures for weekly deep discounts and deliver them to their customers by inserting them in newspapers in the morning. The client's competitors are also doing the same and the problem is that this scheme is not generating enough return on investment for our client as compared to competitors.
prompt.question: How would you analyze the situation to see where the problem could be and how would you compare the execution strategy of offering these discounts of our client with that of their competitors?

clarifying_info.q: On what days are the client's discount campaigns run relative to competitors?
clarifying_info.a: Campaigns are run on the same day as competitors.

clarifying_info.q: How accessible are the client's stores compared to competitors?
clarifying_info.a: Stores are as accessible, if not more so, than competitors.

clarifying_info.q: Is the client's product mix similar to competitors?
clarifying_info.a: Store product-mix is similar to competitors.

clarifying_info.q: How do the client's discounts compare to competitors in terms of price and product?
clarifying_info.a: Our discounts are similar to those of our competitors in price and product.

clarifying_info.q: Which newspapers is the client using to distribute brochures?
clarifying_info.a: We are using the same newspapers as our competitors.

framework: Getting customers into stores: examine discount timing vs. competitors (day of week), brochure layout and newspaper selection, store accessibility

Servicing customers once inside the store: in-store customer service levels on sale days, inventory management for high-demand sale items, in-store pricing accuracy and system updates, capturing additional revenue from non-discounted products
Planning and analysis: supply chain communication to suppliers about anticipated demand shifts, retroactive demand analysis to identify most effective sales
Bundling and upsell strategy: pairing discounted items with full-price complementary products to increase basket size

questions.prompt: On what days are the campaigns run and which newspaper is used? How does brochure layout compare to competitors?
questions.guidance: Candidate should probe whether the timing, channel, and presentation of the brochure are differentiated. Even if the same newspaper is used, layout quality and position within the newspaper can affect customer reach and response rates. These are ruled out as root causes given the clarifying information, but a strong candidate raises them systematically.

questions.prompt: Once customers are in the store, what operational issues could reduce ROI from discount campaigns?
questions.guidance: The primary issue identified in the case: in-store price systems were NOT updated to reflect discounts, causing a discrepancy between the brochure price and the price shown at checkout. This confused customers severely and undermined the ROI of the campaign. Candidate should also address service levels (enough staff?), inventory levels (stocked out on discounted items?), and upsell of full-price items.

questions.prompt: How can the client improve supply chain and inventory management around sale periods?
questions.guidance: Client should use electronic communication along the supply chain to alert suppliers to anticipated demand shifts well in advance, enabling appropriate restocking. Retroactive demand analysis (which sales generated the most gross revenue lift) should guide which products to discount in future campaigns.

brainstorming.prompt: How do we sell non-discounted products to people entering the store purely for discounted items, and how do we determine which items to feature in newspaper inserts?

categories.name: Bundling
ideas: Discount a high-traffic item (e.g., hamburger meat) and place complementary full-price items nearby (buns, ketchup, mustard, relish, tablecloths, paper plates)
Bundle salad dressing, dessert toppings, or beverages near discounted centerpiece items
Create themed sale groupings (BBQ bundle, breakfast bundle) to drive full-price attachment

categories.name: Store Layout & Merchandising
ideas: Place discounted items at the back of the store so customers pass full-price items on the way
Use endcap displays to feature full-margin items adjacent to the discounted zone
Signage that highlights complementary products next to discounted items

categories.name: Timing & Channel
ideas: Evaluate whether running campaigns on Friday vs. Saturday changes foot traffic and conversion
Test different newspaper sections or front-of-insert placement to increase brochure visibility
Digital channels (email, app) as supplement to newspaper brochures to reach targeted segments

categories.name: Operational Readiness
ideas: Ensure all in-store price systems are updated before store opens on sale day
Brief customer service staff on sale items and anticipated questions
Pre-position additional stock of discounted SKUs to avoid stockouts during peak hours

recommendation: The primary root cause of underperformance is an operational failure: in-store pricing systems were not updated to reflect the advertised discounts, creating customer confusion and eroding trust and conversion
To fix this, implement a pre-sale system checklist that verifies all POS and shelf price tags reflect brochure prices before stores open on discount days
Layer on bundling strategies to increase basket size among customers who enter specifically for discounted items
risks: Operational fix requires coordination across 120 stores and may require IT investment to streamline price-update workflows
Bundling effectiveness depends on product placement strategy and may require store layout changes
If competitors adopt similar bundling, the incremental revenue benefit may erode over time
next_steps: Audit current POS price-update process and identify failure points across all 120 stores
Pilot a bundling layout in a subset of stores during the next campaign and measure basket size lift
Conduct retroactive demand analysis on past campaigns to prioritize highest-ROI discount items for future brochures
Establish electronic supply chain alerts to suppliers ahead of each campaign to prevent stockouts
